\begin{scripture}[Proverbs][24]
\lettrine[lines=4]{B}{e} not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.
\vs{2}For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.
\vs{3}Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:
\vs{4}And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.
\vs{5}A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.
\vs{6}For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors there is safety.
\vs{7}Wisdom is too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.
\vs{8}He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.
\vs{9}The thought of foolishness is sin: and the scorner is an abomination to men.
\vs{10}If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.
\vs{11}If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;
\vs{12}If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?
\vs{13}My son, eat thou honey, because it is good; and the honeycomb, which is sweet to thy taste:
\vs{14}So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
\vs{15}Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:
\vs{16}For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
\vs{17}Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:
\vs{18}Lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
\vs{19}Fret not thyself because of evil men, neither be thou envious at the wicked:
\vs{20}For there shall be no reward to the evil man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.
\vs{21}My son, fear thou the LORD and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change:
\vs{22}For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?
\vs{23}These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.
\vs{24}He that saith unto the wicked, Thou are righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:
\vs{25}But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.
\vs{26}Every man shall kiss his lips that giveth a right answer.
\vs{27}Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.
\vs{28}Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive not with thy lips.
\vs{29}Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.
\vs{30}I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
\vs{31}And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
\vs{32}Then I saw, and considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction.
\vs{33}Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
\vs{34}So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.
\end{scripture}

##### Chapter 25

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Proverbs" data-chapter="25">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>hese are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out. <span class="verse-number">2</span> It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter. <span class="verse-number">3</span> The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men: <span class="verse-number">7</span> For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another: <span class="verse-number">10</span> Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away. <span class="verse-number">11</span> A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver. <span class="verse-number">12</span> As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear. <span class="verse-number">13</span> As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain. <span class="verse-number">15</span> By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone. <span class="verse-number">16</span> Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it. <span class="verse-number">17</span> Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee. <span class="verse-number">18</span> A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow. <span class="verse-number">19</span> Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint. <span class="verse-number">20</span> As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart. <span class="verse-number">21</span> If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: <span class="verse-number">22</span> For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee. <span class="verse-number">23</span> The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue. <span class="verse-number">24</span> It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house. <span class="verse-number">25</span> As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country. <span class="verse-number">26</span> A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring. <span class="verse-number">27</span> It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory. <span class="verse-number">28</span> He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.</p>
</div>
:::

##### Chapter 26

##### Chapter 27

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Proverbs" data-chapter="27">
<p><span class="drop-cap">B</span>oast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth. <span class="verse-number">2</span> Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips. <span class="verse-number">3</span> A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath is heavier than them both. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy? <span class="verse-number">5</span> Open rebuke is better than secret love. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful. <span class="verse-number">7</span> The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet. <span class="verse-number">8</span> As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off. <span class="verse-number">11</span> My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me. <span class="verse-number">12</span> A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished. <span class="verse-number">13</span> Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman. <span class="verse-number">14</span> He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him. <span class="verse-number">15</span> A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike. <span class="verse-number">16</span> Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself. <span class="verse-number">17</span> Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend. <span class="verse-number">18</span> Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured. <span class="verse-number">19</span> As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied. <span class="verse-number">21</span> As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise. <span class="verse-number">22</span> Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him. <span class="verse-number">23</span> Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds. <span class="verse-number">24</span> For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation? <span class="verse-number">25</span> The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered. <span class="verse-number">26</span> The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field. <span class="verse-number">27</span> And thou shalt have goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.</p>
</div>

##### Chapter 28

<div class="scripture" data-book="Proverbs" data-chapter="28">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>he wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion. <span class="verse-number">2</span> For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged. <span class="verse-number">3</span> A poor man that oppresseth the poor is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food. <span class="verse-number">4</span> They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them. <span class="verse-number">5</span> Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all things. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous men shameth his father. <span class="verse-number">8</span> He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor. <span class="verse-number">9</span> He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession. <span class="verse-number">11</span> The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out. <span class="verse-number">12</span> When righteous men do rejoice, there is great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden. <span class="verse-number">13</span> He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy. <span class="verse-number">14</span> Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief. <span class="verse-number">15</span> As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people. <span class="verse-number">16</span> The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor: but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days. <span class="verse-number">17</span> A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him. <span class="verse-number">18</span> Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once. <span class="verse-number">19</span> He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough. <span class="verse-number">20</span> A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent. <span class="verse-number">21</span> To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress. <span class="verse-number">22</span> He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him. <span class="verse-number">23</span> He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue. <span class="verse-number">24</span> Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer. <span class="verse-number">25</span> He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat. <span class="verse-number">26</span> He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered. <span class="verse-number">27</span> He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse. <span class="verse-number">28</span> When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.</p>
</div>

##### Chapter 30

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Proverbs" data-chapter="30">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>he words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal, <span class="verse-number">2</span> Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man. <span class="verse-number">3</span> I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy. <span class="verse-number">4</span> Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell? <span class="verse-number">5</span> Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die: <span class="verse-number">8</span> Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: <span class="verse-number">9</span> Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the LORD? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Accuse not a servant unto his master, lest he curse thee, and thou be found guilty. <span class="verse-number">11</span> There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother. <span class="verse-number">12</span> There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, and yet is not washed from their filthiness. <span class="verse-number">13</span> There is a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up. <span class="verse-number">14</span> There is a generation, whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men. <span class="verse-number">15</span> The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, yea, four things say not, It is enough: <span class="verse-number">16</span> The grave; and the barren womb; the earth that is not filled with water; and the fire that saith not, It is enough. <span class="verse-number">17</span> The eye that mocketh at his father, and despiseth to obey his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it. <span class="verse-number">18</span> There be three things which are too wonderful for me, yea, four which I know not: <span class="verse-number">19</span> The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a serpent upon a rock; the way of a ship in the midst of the sea; and the way of a man with a maid. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness. <span class="verse-number">21</span> For three things the earth is disquieted, and for four which it cannot bear: <span class="verse-number">22</span> For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled with meat; <span class="verse-number">23</span> For an odious woman when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress. <span class="verse-number">24</span> There be four things which are little upon the earth, but they are exceeding wise: <span class="verse-number">25</span> The ants are a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer; <span class="verse-number">26</span> The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks; <span class="verse-number">27</span> The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands; <span class="verse-number">28</span> The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces. <span class="verse-number">29</span> There be three things which go well, yea, four are comely in going: <span class="verse-number">30</span> A lion which is strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any; <span class="verse-number">31</span> A greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom there is no rising up. <span class="verse-number">32</span> If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, or if thou hast thought evil, lay thine hand upon thy mouth. <span class="verse-number">33</span> Surely the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, and the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood: so the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.</p>
</div>

\begin{scripture}[Proverbs][30]
\lettrine[lines=4]{T}{he} words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,
\vs{2}Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man.
\vs{3}I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy.
\vs{4}Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell?
\vs{5}Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him.
\vs{6}Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.
\vs{7}Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die:
\vs{8}Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:
\vs{9}Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the LORD? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.
\vs{10}Accuse not a servant unto his master, lest he curse thee, and thou be found guilty.
\vs{11}There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.
\vs{12}There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, and yet is not washed from their filthiness.
\vs{13}There is a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up.
\vs{14}There is a generation, whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.
\vs{15}The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, yea, four things say not, It is enough:
\vs{16}The grave; and the barren womb; the earth that is not filled with water; and the fire that saith not, It is enough.
\vs{17}The eye that mocketh at his father, and despiseth to obey his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.
\vs{18}There be three things which are too wonderful for me, yea, four which I know not:
\vs{19}The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a serpent upon a rock; the way of a ship in the midst of the sea; and the way of a man with a maid.
\vs{20}Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.
\vs{21}For three things the earth is disquieted, and for four which it cannot bear:
\vs{22}For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled with meat;
\vs{23}For an odious woman when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress.
\vs{24}There be four things which are little upon the earth, but they are exceeding wise:
\vs{25}The ants are a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer;
\vs{26}The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks;
\vs{27}The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands;
\vs{28}The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces.
\vs{29}There be three things which go well, yea, four are comely in going:
\vs{30}A lion which is strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any;
\vs{31}A greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom there is no rising up.

##### Chapter 31

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Proverbs" data-chapter="31">
<p><span class="drop-cap">T</span>he words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him. <span class="verse-number">2</span> What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows? <span class="verse-number">3</span> Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings. <span class="verse-number">4</span> It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink: <span class="verse-number">5</span> Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted. <span class="verse-number">6</span> Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts. <span class="verse-number">7</span> Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction. <span class="verse-number">9</span> Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy. <span class="verse-number">10</span> Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies. <span class="verse-number">11</span> The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil. <span class="verse-number">12</span> She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life. <span class="verse-number">13</span> She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands. <span class="verse-number">14</span> She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar. <span class="verse-number">15</span> She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens. <span class="verse-number">16</span> She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard. <span class="verse-number">17</span> She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms. <span class="verse-number">18</span> She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night. <span class="verse-number">19</span> She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff. <span class="verse-number">20</span> She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy. <span class="verse-number">21</span> She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet. <span class="verse-number">22</span> She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple. <span class="verse-number">23</span> Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land. <span class="verse-number">24</span> She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant. <span class="verse-number">25</span> Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come. <span class="verse-number">26</span> She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness. <span class="verse-number">27</span> She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness. <span class="verse-number">28</span> Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her. <span class="verse-number">29</span> Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all. <span class="verse-number">30</span> Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised. <span class="verse-number">31</span> Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.</p>
</div>

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
\begin{scripture}[Proverbs][31]
\lettrine[lines=4]{T}{he} words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him.
\vs{2}What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows?
\vs{3}Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.
\vs{4}It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:
\vs{5}Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.
\vs{6}Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts.
\vs{7}Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
\vs{8}Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.
\vs{9}Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
\vs{10}Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
\vs{11}The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.
\vs{12}She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.
\vs{13}She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.
\vs{14}She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar.
\vs{15}She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.
\vs{16}She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.
\vs{17}She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.
\vs{18}She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night.
\vs{19}She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.
\vs{20}She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.
\vs{21}She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
\vs{22}She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.
\vs{23}Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.
\vs{24}She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
\vs{25}Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
\vs{26}She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.
\vs{27}She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.
\vs{28}Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.
\vs{29}Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.
\vs{30}Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
\vs{31}Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.
\end{scripture}
